issues.message: Exponential backtracking (proven). Severity: CRITICAL, confidence: HIGH.
issues.hint: Attack: "<IFRAME" . "\"\"\"\"" x n . "!<iframe" Replayed on PCRE2 10.49: preg_match fails from length 5003 (backtrack_limit 100000, JIT off). The risky part is: "[^"]*"|'[^']*'|[^>] Hotspot offsets: 11-31 Overlapping alternation branches inside a quantifier. e.g. (a|a)* or (ab|a)*. This can lead to catastrophic backtracking. Suggested (verify behavior): Make alternatives mutually exclusive or order longer alternatives first. Test with adversarial inputs like repeated strings followed by a non-matching character.

issues.message: Nested quantifiers can cause catastrophic backtracking.
issues.hint: Consider atomic groups (?>...) or possessive quantifiers — verify the rewrite still matches everything you need.

issues.message: Alternation branches ""[^"]*"" and "[^>]" have overlapping character sets, which may cause unnecessary backtracking.
issues.hint: Consider using atomic groups (?>...) to prevent backtracking. Do not reorder overlapping alternatives as it changes match semantics.
